comment: mixz file-format registry, read by mixz.py for format v2. APPEND ONLY from the first public release: never change, remove or reuse an entry, because stored files refer to these IDs; tools/test_roundtrip.py checks every head listed in 'heads'. Before that release the registry is a draft: entries of dropped pre-release codecs are removed, their IDs are listed in 'retired' and never reused (so such a file fails at its header), the current codec's engine_sha256 is updated after output-neutral engine edits (tests/check_vectors.py proves the output unchanged), and 'heads' restarts with the current head. A version is everything the decoder needs besides the file's own header: the codec (engine algorithm, identified by the sha256 of its source file), the engine profile (which context set the codec uses), the mind modules replayed before the data (checked by sha256 when loaded; replayed in list order) and the mixer start weights (null: the codec's built-in start values). A version's identity is its content hash (mixz.version_hash): the sha256 of those parts, so it means the same on every machine. Short IDs are aliases issued only here; a file can instead name a version by its hash (ID 0 followed by 16 hash bytes), which any registry or store holding that content can resolve. A profile is the detected content type; it is informational, and decoding never depends on it. A deflate is the implementation used to re-create gzip and PNG streams. 'source' and 'prefix' tell mixz.py where a codec's code is and what its exported functions are called.

3.name: cm3
3.description: Codec 2 (the MVP model: 8 hashed context models, 8 run models, an order-0 model, a match model, 4 gated mixers plus a final mixer, 2 APM stages, a 32-bit binary arithmetic coder; 16-bit first-layer mixer weights with AVX2 multiply-add and an identical scalar path) plus two text engine profiles, code (contexts 0, 1 and 6 replaced by line indentation, last punctuation and bracket nesting) and web (contexts 1 and 7 replaced by bracket nesting and the HTML tag), and a 2-byte shortest match for the image profile; plan step 6.
